key_insight: PhysDial shows that learned PDE simulators respond more faithfully to changing physical conditions when training includes trajectories that diverge after an intervention.
engineering_relevance: More reliable predictions after forcing or parameter changes could support fluid-flow control, design exploration, and what-if studies.
method: Adapt a pretrained video diffusion transformer to eight 2D PDE families.
Encode coefficients alongside noise level, condition fields as reference frames, and equation text as prompts.
Train with within-trajectory switches and evaluate against changed solver branches from the same state.
evidence_signal: In Kolmogorov flow, within-trajectory switches comprised about 5% of training samples and halved post-change error at matched compute for forcing-wavenumber or amplitude changes.
watch_item: Results cover 2D PDEs; robustness to unseen interventions and transfer to 3D engineering flows remain unestablished.
paper_title: PhysDial: Adapting Pretrained Video Models for PDE Simulation under Changing Physical Conditions
